name: Kyriakos Mitsotakis
role: Prime Minister of the Hellenic Republic (Πρωθυπουργός της Ελληνικής Δημοκρατίας)
party: Νέα Δημοκρατία / New Democracy (ND) — European People's Party (EPP)
bio: Kyriakos Mitsotakis (Κυριάκος Μητσοτάκης), born in Athens on 4 March 1968, has been Prime Minister of Greece since 8 July 2019, apart from a caretaker interlude between the May and June 2023 elections, and has led New Democracy (ND) since January 2016. The son of former Prime Minister Konstantinos Mitsotakis and a graduate of Harvard and Stanford, he worked in banking, consulting and venture capital before being elected MP for Athens B in 2004, and was Minister of Administrative Reform and e-Governance from 2013 to 2015. He won the July 2019 election with 39.85% of the vote and 158 of 300 seats and, after the May 2023 vote produced no majority, was re-elected in June 2023 with 40.56% and again 158 seats. His governments have overseen Greece's return to investment grade (completed when Moody's upgraded the country in March 2025), tax cuts and successive minimum-wage rises, the legalisation of same-sex civil marriage in 2024 and a harder line on migration, while facing the 2022 wiretapping scandal, the Tempi rail disaster of February 2023 and the EU-funded farm-subsidy fraud investigated by the European Public Prosecutor's Office, which led to ministerial resignations in 2025 and April 2026. As of October 2026 he heads a single-party ND government ahead of the parliamentary election due in 2027; a constitutional revision backed by his majority, including changes to Article 86 on ministerial criminal liability and Article 16 on universities, now awaits the next parliament.
